notes: Eleven title memberships independently checked. Conditional partial drafting follows the assigned reconciliation standard and is an inference rather than explicit listed permission. The policy’s series-of-prompts prohibition remains ambiguous at the boundary.

The legacy US policy URL redirected to the current policy during this check; it is not independent corroboration. Public Policy and Administration live instructions timed out twice; the accessible Sage PDF and indexed live instructions refer to Sage AI policy, with potential PDF staleness.

patches.audit_note: Independently read journal instructions and current Sage policy. Original classification compatible; conditional drafting is a semantic inference, not an express drafting permission. No stricter title-specific AI ban was identified in the inspected instructions.

ai_policy.summary: Human-led literature assistance and generated or checked research code are expressly listed as appropriate subject to disclosure. Conditional partial substantive drafting is inferred from the treatment of primary or partial generated text, the statement that disclosed use alone is not grounds for rejection, and the non-exhaustive examples; the policy does not expressly list drafting as an appropriate example. Authors remain responsible for accuracy and original sources.

disclosure.instructions: Disclose generated content that directly affects methodology, analysis, results or conclusions upon submission for editorial evaluation; appropriate research uses are disclosed in methods or acknowledgements. Suggestions to improve the author’s language, grammar or structure need no disclosure. Verify outputs and original sources.

restrictions: Sage lists generation of data or a submission using a series of prompts as inappropriate. Its wording does not define the boundary for partial human-led drafting; avoid an entirely prompt-generated submission and seek clarification for borderline uses.

Do not list AI chatbots as authors.

findings: Health Information Management Journal and Medical Care Research and Review were previously prohibited solely from a broad interpretation of Sage’s series-of-prompts clause; their inspected instructions do not establish a separate title-specific drafting ban. Recommend conditional compatibility under the assigned interpretation.

Perspectives in Public Health, Public Policy and Administration and The American Review of Public Administration were previously unclear; the combined Sage policy clauses support conditional drafting under the assigned standard. PPA applicability rests on the official PDF and indexed live text because direct live retrieval timed out.
The Sage wording does not define whether partial drafting with several prompts falls under its prohibited submission-generation clause; this material ambiguity must remain visible.
